title: 943rd Rescue Group Mission Video 2017
description:
Mission - The 943rd Rescue Group organizes, trains and equips mission ready citizen airmen to perform personnel recovery operations worldwide.

Vision - The 943rd Rescue Group will be a premier Combat Rescue Organization providing world class combat ready Citizen Airmen and resources to the ever changing national security environment, anytime, anywhere.

transcript.text: - [Female] In days long past, the hero Bellerophon rose high
into the clouds upon the back of mighty Pegasus.
Lean stallion of the gods, carrying lightening
and thunder from Mount Olympus.
Pegasus destroyed his enemies,
and with a torrent wind from his mighty wings,
carried heroes away to the sky.
(preparing-for-action drum music)
- [Male] The global mission of the United States Air Force
requires the ability to recover personnel
anywhere, anytime.
The men and women of the Air Force Reserve
serving at the 943rd Rescue Group
are some of the most elite special operation warriors
in the U.S. military.
Pilots and flight engineers operate side by side
with para rescue jumpers, SERE specialists,
and combat rescue officers who form a specialized
human weapon system known as Guardian Angel,
a unique capability to ensure the recovery
of personnel.
The 943rd Rescue Group at Davis-Monthan Air Force Base
in Arizona, which includes the 304th Rescue Squadron
in Oregon, operates HH-60 Pave Hawk helicopters
and other highly modified vehicles to perform
combat or rescue missions in any environment.
We've supported efforts throughout
the Middle East and Africa.
We've aided U.S. Homeland defense
and assisted domestic rescue efforts as needed.
Our doctors and combat medics train and specialize
in the most advanced life-saving techniques,
while our aircraft maintenance and support personnel
enable the rescue mission stateside and deployed.
The personnel support specialist and facilities
at the 943rd provide the best care and assistance available,
allowing these skilled specialists to focus
on constant training and mission preparedness.
Our citizen airmen balance the demands
of civilian and military life to perform one of the most
advanced capabilities in the Air Force.
Together, with our parent unit, the 920th Rescue Wing
at Patrick Air Force Base, Florida, we've saved
more than 3,000 lives, including 1,200 combat saves.
Our great winged mascot inspires our mission.
To defeat our enemies, reach out to our nation's heroes,
and lift them to safety.
